THE RECESS CLIP (NEW, and the run's hardest-won lesson): a recess viewed obliquely hides a band of its own floor equal to the recess depth's screen projection, so drawing the floor and walls unclipped makes every groove read as a raised BLOCK sitting on the surface. Clip all recess interiors to the OPENING polygon. Three pixel critics independently reported the inverted read before the cause was found.

entries.hero_structure: THE HOUR COLUMN (NEW): a vertical two-material quantity column standing on a wet boat deck under ONE orthographic GPU camera, built so that one world unit is one hour at a printed, constant 14.0 px per hour. The bottom 7 hours render as BRUSHED STEEL (the natural window a fish has always had) and the 53 hours above as POLISHED BRASS (the manufactured window). The MATERIAL CHANGE AT THE 7 HOUR LINE is the thesis with zero words. Orthographic because the slide draws a QUANTITY and doctrine bars perspective on quantities. The column is the hero on only 2 of 9 slides (a close detail crop on the cover, the full measured object on S03), so it is deliberately NOT deck 17's one-object-under-one-camera register. NOT a rendered gold authority seal (15), NOT the Adjudicated Margin op-ed chassis with a pen (16), NOT the milled bone limestone register (17), NOT the dead-end insulator string on a yoke plate (18).
entries.atmosphere: SODIUM ON SILT: a warm sodium deck lamp (az 118, el 55, key to fill about 5 to 1) over warm brown-black glacial silt (#1A140D / #241B12 / #4A3218), CLEAR AIR with no fog anywhere, and cold confined to exactly one material in the deck, the slush ice. Dark ground (the one light-deck-per-8-runs allowance was spent on 2026-07-25). Deliberately warm-dominant to escape deck 18's cold low-chroma graphite-teal sea fog on wet steel, which was the trap the field-documentarian director was the only one to price. NOT op-ed warm ink-black paper (16), NOT gallery-lit bone (17), NOT sea fog on wet steel (18).

entries.post_score_repair_note: The material change at hour 7 did NOT fully render. Under a single 0xffb067 sodium key, steel at 0xb9bcbd and brass at 0xd39c31 both read as one amber extrusion at feed scale. The repair pass lifted the steel to 0xe8edf0 at roughness 0.62 and added a proud collar at the seam so the change reads as a joint rather than a gradient; darkening the brass to force contrast made the frame muddier and was reverted. The encoding now reads better but not fully. Two materials separated only by hue collapse under a strongly coloured key: separate by value and by a physical joint.
entries.plate_system_note: Every mono knockout and chip in this deck was hand-sized at roughly 14px per character against JetBrains Mono's actual 16.8px at 24px with 0.10em tracking. Six labels shipped past their own plates into the scorer. Future decks must compute plate width as 16.8 x charcount + 2 x padding; render.py and qa.py now gate this automatically.

entries.hero_structure: THE INHABITED DARK (NEW): a single Interior Alaska winter valley at night as a five-plane multiplane field, revisited from nine camera stations, where every light source in the world is human. entries.atmosphere: ICE FOG AT FORTY BELOW. Cold high-chroma blues, snow as the major surface, warm cream only where a person is awake. NOT gallery-lit bone (17), NOT sea fog on wet steel (18), NOT sodium amber on glacial silt (19). Dark ground.
entries.depth_technique: AK3D-style ridged heightfield ranges inside a multiplane stack, four parallax rates against a shared global x so the planes seam exactly without a 9720px canvas, ice fog slab with stipple, banded drift filled light-to-dark along its own contour, AKPOST.grade with IGN dither on every art canvas. entries.hero_structure: THE ENGRAVED INSTRUMENT (NEW). A lit paper sheet on a copy stand under one raking key, carrying WHITE-LINE INTAGLIO, revisited at ten stations. The hero (S05) is the 2006 certificate whose guilloche rosette IS the vote, an epitrochoid with R = 113.130 (the YES count scaled 1000 to 1), r = 41.836 (the NO count), d = 73.00 (the percentage as the tracing arm) and 73 turns, so R/r = 2.7042 and the curve never closes. NOT the milled bone limestone register (17), NOT the GPU PBR dead-end insulator string (18), NOT the orthographic Hour Column (19), NOT the Inhabited Dark winter valley multiplane (20). All three treatment directors independently chose line engraving without seeing each other's pitches, the strongest convergence the room has produced in twenty runs.

NOT sea fog on wet steel (18), NOT sodium amber on glacial silt (19), NOT ice fog at forty below (20), and deliberately NOT the series' default cold arctic navy the scorer marked No.20 down for.
entries.depth_technique: WHITE-LINE INTAGLIO via the new assets/js/akengrave.js. Cut lines print LIGHT against a solid inked field, the dark register's native form of line engraving, which keeps the deck out of the barred light ground (the one-light-deck-per-8-runs allowance was spent 2026-07-25). Four engraver's rules implemented rather than described. The lay wraps the form, direction = rot90 of the height field's gradient, so the direction field IS the modelling. The swelled line, every stroke a filled tapered polygon and never a stroked path. Three separately controllable channels, mainline, crossline, interdot, which is a per-region detail budget expressed as a drawing system. Thickness is a lighting decision made per stroke, so lines fatten in shadow and thin toward the key. HERO SHIPPED FLAT AND ARGUED IT rather than climbing to akthree, because all three directors flagged that hairline engraving resampled onto a mesh by a software GPU averages to flat gray, which is No.19's failure in a new material; the relief substrate shares the hero's height field so the form shading and the lay cannot disagree.
entries.line_voice: THE BURIN (NEW). The drafting bench that carried 17, 18 and 19 stays retired. Weight is set by light per stroke, quantized to the five-token ladder for anything that is not a lay line. Crossline enters only where tone is below 0.45, interdot only below 0.22.

entries.hero_structure: THE UNFILLED SHEET (NEW). One true-projection Alaska (conic equal area, parallels 55/65, rotate 154) rendered as an Imhof-manner relief sheet and revisited from eight camera stations, with all 29 boroughs and census areas drawn as cased hairlines and EVERY ONE LEFT UNFILLED, because no source says where the 3,048 live. One gold point, at Anchorage's true projected coordinate. The map is not a locator inset; it is larger than the frame at every station but the close, it carries all the deck's tone, and the deck's central fact is a property of the map itself.
entries.atmosphere: HIGH-ALTITUDE SHEET LIGHT. NO fog layer anywhere in the deck. Depth comes from Imhof's aerial perspective as a VALUE rule keyed to elevation and from nothing else. entries.depth_technique: Imhof Swiss-manner relief implemented directly against noise.js rather than through akrelief, because akrelief exposes no median generaliser and no post-Lambert contrast hook and both ARE the Swiss manner. Heightfield defined in STATION-A SCREEN SPACE so every station shades the same terrain; 3x3 MEDIAN x2 then 50 pct fade back (a median preserves ridge and canyon definition where a blur smears them); 3x3 Sobel normals at strength 13.0; three-light aspect-weighted Lambert (az 315/270/360 at el 38/30/30); elevation-keyed contrast rule; two-stop ramp clamped 3 to 90 pct. Bathymetric contours via d3.contours in the water. Zero WebGL, so the post-GL grade penalty is retired by construction.

entries.notes: THE RUN'S OWN CRAFT RULE CAUSED THE RUN'S OWN RECURRING DEFECT. The dossier's elevation-keyed contrast rule damped the flats to 45 pct of contrast; in this projection the ranges sit mid-frame and the bottom third is Gulf water and peninsula lowland, so the rule itself produced the dead lower third and failed frame_balance on three slides. Raising the floor to 0.62 fixed the dead band and, per the scorer, traded it for a flat one. The heightfield also ran at 3.4 noise units across a 1080px frame, so the Sobel returned near-flat normals and the state shaded as one pale mass until a detail octave and strength 13.0 went in.

entries.hero_structure: THE POSTING LANES (NEW). A fixed, flat, parallel-projection instrument bed. A 770 px rail runs 20 July to 24 August at a printed, constant 22.0 px per day; notice lanes are cabinet-extruded bars on it, each starting at its posting date and terminating in a raised gate block at its closing date. THE CAMERA NEVER MOVES, on any of the ten slides, which is how this breaks the one-object-N-camera-stations shape shared by No.19, No.21 and No.22 by construction rather than by argument. Craft spends across four subjects (the lane bed, the eight-plate fan, the Eielson ground, the posting board slab) plus the search register. NOT the Hour Column (19), NOT the Inhabited Dark (20), NOT the Engraved Instrument (21), NOT the Unfilled Sheet (22).
entries.atmosphere: LOW-ANGLE TERMINAL GLOW. Clear air. No fog, no veil, no haze, no volumetric shaft and no horizon anywhere in ten slides. One low key behind and below the bed at azimuth 205 elevation 22, so every lane wall is backlit at its top bevel and throws a short forward two-part contact shadow. NOT ice fog at forty below (20), NOT copy-stand rake (21), NOT high-altitude sheet light (22).

entries.hero_structure: THE HEAD SHEET (NEW). A ten-sheet orthographic DRAWING SET with zero obliquity anywhere, magnification changing across sheets from 1:24,000 (profile) to 1:200 (dam elevation and section) to 1:4 (the valve full section). The camera never orbits and never pans a landscape, it changes MAGNIFICATION AND DRAWING TYPE, which is what a drawing set does and what a camera cannot. NOT the Engraved Instrument (21, no paper, no copy stand, no intaglio), NOT the Unfilled Sheet (22, one 180px locator inset never revisited, geography is not the protagonist), NOT the Posting Lanes (23, orthographic true section rather than cabinet oblique, and the magnification moves), NOT the Cut Block (24, a section is a plane with no thickness, nothing to extrude and nothing to see obliquely).

entries.notes: THE MECHANISM REFUSES TO RENDER A PROJECTION, and this is the run's most transferable idea. The winning director proposed encoding the 38 percent as 1.38x streak density inside the same water under the same tonal law, and named the seam that creates in his own self-critique, that a reader who correctly reads head-driven lightness as physics will read the density as physics too and the legend distinguishing them dies first at feed scale. The 38 percent is drawn as phantom dash with zero fill and zero streaks everywhere it appears, so measured and projected can never be confused at any scale, with or without a legend.

entries.hero_structure: THE OPEN BLOCK (NEW). A bound government record on a dark press table, seen from ONE camera that never moves on any of nine slides, at a declared constant 125.0 px per world unit. The narrative is performed by the OBJECT rather than by the lens. NOT the Unfilled Sheet (22, no map, no projection, no geodata anywhere in nine slides), NOT the Posting Lanes (23, no rail, no lane, no gate, no date axis, no lower-band quantity strip), NOT the Cut Block (24, nothing is sectioned and a cut block can't open), NOT the Head Sheet (25, magnification is a declared constant on every slide and there is no drawing set). HONEST CAVEAT, volunteered by the director in its own self-critique rather than found by the scorer: No.21's Engraved Instrument was also paper lit on a work surface in a warm dark room. It is five decks back and outside the forbidden window. The mechanism differs on five axes, a mass rather than a sheet, depth from lamination and occlusion rather than micro-relief, a HIGH key at elevation 68 rather than a rake, no intaglio, and a frozen camera rather than ten stations. The family resemblance is still real and is recorded here rather than argued away.

entries.hero_structure: THE UNBOUNDED POPULATION (NEW). A field of identical registration cards on pure void, with NO object, NO ground plane, NO camera station and NO frame the field is bounded by. The recurring element is a POPULATION rather than a thing, and the field always runs off the right edge so the deck is structurally unable to draw a closed whole. Breaks the family of 24 to 27, all four of which were a bounded object or sheet under a fixed camera.
entries.atmosphere: REPLY AS KEY LIGHT (NEW). There is no external key anywhere in nine slides. Every photon in the deck is emitted by a card that answered, so illumination EQUALS knowledge and the lit fraction of any frame is the measured fraction of its population. The deck's darkest frames are the ones where the record is emptiest, and slide 09 closes by inverting it: the only light left is the gold Polaris, which in this deck means the reader's own available move rather than a reply the state received.
entries.depth_technique: Canvas 2D modelled solids. Every card is a cardPath with one clipped corner, never a bare rect, carrying a two-part contact shadow (a wide blurred pool plus a tight occlusion band) whose silhouette matches the object rather than a rectangle. Stippled paper tooth as arc() discs at every scale so the surfaces survive the zoom test. THE RENDERED LADDER (akthree GPU PBR) WAS DECLARED FOR SLIDE 04 AND NOT REACHED; it shipped on the designed fallback. Log this as a SHORTFALL, not a rung. Fourth deck in six.

shortfalls: THE RENDERED LADDER WAS REACHED, ending a four-in-six failure run. aksdf was chosen structurally, because there is no GL context to fail and therefore no fallback to slide into. Slides 01, 05 and 06 are genuinely raymarched.

THE EVIDENCE CONTRACT FOR IT FAILED FIRST. Luminance probes were authored from PREDICTED screen coordinates instead of measured off a render, landed off the aperture and reported the dark frame as brighter than the lit one. Re-measured off the shipped pixels the aperture falls 98.3 to 26.9 L* and the bed band falls 8.5.
Device C, ONE FISH AT A TIME, built at the 01 to 02 junction only. The flow critic found it at zero of eight junctions on first pass; it is partial at best and should be built or struck next run.

Slide 02's declared Sitka Sound map inset was never coded, so that slide's declared literal anchor is absent. dossier_check returned PASS 9/9 anyway, which means the gate cannot see a declared element that was never built.
Stair-step aliasing on every raymarched edge from the 440x660 and 480x720 internal upscale.
Two critic rounds ran, five pixel critics then a flow critic, and the repairs from both were not re-reviewed.

entries.hero_structure: NEW: THE OPEN TREAD. A stepped instrument on a lit birch floor under an ORTHOGRAPHIC camera at a declared 2.6 px per minute, where each tread's RUN is a published minute cap and the fifth tread has no material at all, 419 px of floor visible through it. World X maps to screen x at exactly 1:1 for any tilt, which is the honesty guarantee. Diverges from THE OPEN BLOCK (26, no paper, no table, and the camera is parallel not fixed-perspective), THE TRAVERSE (27, nothing travels, the instrument stays put), THE UNBOUNDED POPULATION (28, one bounded object on a lit ground, not a population on void) and THE LIT APERTURE (29, the gap is the only place with NO material seen in flat daylight, the exact inversion).

entries.hero_structure: NEW: THE FALLING FRAME. The deck's variable is SCALE ITSELF. Nine slides descend from a measured 670 km sheet to twenty feet of powerhouse floor and climb back to the same 670 km sheet, and the scale rail relabels at every rung: km, km, km, km oblique, 1 FT = 42 PX, 1 MW = 42.6 PX, a count with NO scale, dollars, km. Diverges from the whole 24-to-30 family, which held scale constant under one camera; here the camera's ground sampling distance is the argument. Against the forbidden four: not THE TRAVERSE (27), nothing travels; not THE UNBOUNDED POPULATION (28), though slide 07 borrows that structure for ONE slide and it is not the hero; not THE LIT APERTURE (29); not THE OPEN TREAD (30), which was one instrument at one scale.

entries.twenty_foot_lock: 1 ft = 42 px, deck-wide. Slide 05's 3D rig is SOLVED FROM THE LOCK: one world unit is one foot and the camera distance is computed so one foot is 42 screen px, so the dimension and the room are produced by the same number and cannot disagree. Slide 06's busbar baseline is 840 px, the chart is literally twenty feet wide. Slide 07's ISOTYPE pitch is 42 px, one microgrid per foot. Slide 08 inherits slide 05's rig byte for byte, which is what makes its substitution provable rather than asserted.

entries.hero_structure: NEW: THE LOCKED CHASE. A letterpress composing stone under one raking work lamp, seen at a fixed 30 degrees for all nine slides. In printing, FURNITURE is the trade's literal name for the blank material that fills a page and takes no ink, which is exactly what this story is about, form occupying the space where labor should be. Two of three directors arrived at this object independently. Diverges from THE UNBOUNDED POPULATION (28) by being one bounded iron frame whose function is to lock things in, with every object in contact and casting a two-part shadow; from THE LIT APERTURE (29) by firing no SDF and no GPU path at all, its brightest region a wet-ink specular on an opaque face; from THE OPEN TREAD (30) because nothing is stepped and every block is the same height, since type-high is a real physical constant; and from THE FALLING FRAME (31) because scale is held rigidly constant deck-wide and the constancy is the point.
entries.atmosphere: NEW: LOCKUP RAKE. The light a compositor actually uses to check that a forme is locked and type-high. Single hard work lamp, key azimuth 292 elevation 24, key to fill 6 to 1, warm sodium key against a cold steel bounce, no fog and no volumetric term anywhere. Elevation 24 is a craft decision rather than a mood: akengrave sets stroke width from pow(1-ndotl,1.6), so the 20 to 30 band spreads ndotl across nearly its full range and the swelled line is legible instead of a uniform hatch.
continuity_devices: THE INKLESS SLUG, a piece of furniture standing type-high where a byline slug would go, carrying no printing face. It gains a desk name and a blank name line on 02, is camouflaged by company on 04, is ABSENT on 06 where the turn lands, and returns gold faced carrying the ask on 09.

THE DATELINE ADVANCE, a raised dateline block upper right whose date is the progress meter, coupled to a newsprint temperature drift from #E8E2D2 down to #D5D2C8 so the last warm paper in the deck is the last proof pulled.

It EXONERATES the subject and indicts the system around it, which is the opposite emotional motion from THE DISQUALIFYING VIRTUE (29), and it is declarative rather than interrogative unlike 31.

entries.depth_technique: akengrave (#93) as the primary bench on all nine slides, its own library entry recording that five consecutive decks failed to use it while artwork craft was weakest in four of them. Every form is precomputed into a 4px bilinear lookup grid because normalAt calls form four times per sample. NO GPU path anywhere, so no webglOK fallback and no black-frame sentinel risk. Depth comes from cabinet extrusion, two-part contact shadows cast onto deliberately lit pools, scale gradient, atmospheric falloff and a blurred repoussoir lip drawn once offscreen.
entries.note: THE LESSON OF THE RUN IS THAT form MUST BE SMOOTH. The first slide-01 build used max(|dx|,|dy|) as its height field and the lay came out as concentric rectangles, a digital artifact rather than metal. The second used high-frequency fbm and the lay came out as marbling, because the lay's DIRECTION is the gradient of form, so any high frequency term rotates it per pixel. One slow plane plus two broad smooth bumps is what produces the long slowly bending parallels that read as engraving. Recorded because it cost three render rounds.

entries.hero_structure: NEW: THE EQUAL-AWARD PROJECTION. One continuous chart sheet seen square on, where the variable is not the camera and not the subject but the PROJECTION. Every honest map prints a note declaring what it preserves, so this deck prints one and updates it every slide, and on the slides that draw NSF's rule the note has to admit the rule's projection preserves the state count and gives up area. A two-plate print, land in white-line intaglio on a dark sheet, the rule over it in regulated magenta as an overprint. Diverges from THE LIT APERTURE (29) by having no aperture, no raymarcher and no camera translation in z; from THE OPEN TREAD (30) by having no object and no room, the sheet bleeding off all four edges with no datum to stand on; from THE FALLING FRAME (31) by inverting it deliberately, welding the ruler down (one conic equal-area projection, one printed scale bar, one 48 px ring never resized on any slide) so the GEOMETRY is what deforms; and from THE LOCKED CHASE (32) by sitting at 0 degrees with no furniture, no quoins and no wet specular, where a chase locks rectangles into place and a neatline is the thing a coastline refuses to obey. Structurally it is a category break from all four, which were one object under a controlled camera in an interior. This is a POPULATED FIELD of fifty things at true relative area under a parallel projection with no viewpoint to move.
entries.atmosphere: NEW: NEAR-EDGE PLATE LAMP. A single warm lamp clamped at the NEAR edge of a chart table rather than the far corner, so light arrives from below and to the right and the brightest modelled tone in every frame falls in the bottom third by construction. Key azimuth 118, elevation 26, key to fill 2.8 to 1, with the fill a broad bounce off the sheet so no shadow is grey. Elevation 26 sits inside akhachure's legible band of 20 to 30 where ndotl spreads across nearly its full range and the swelled line actually swells. Scatter rather than fog, no volumetric shafts. The three forbidden atmospheres all sit in a 292 to 305 azimuth band, so this deck is lit from roughly 174 degrees away, the opposite side of the sky.

entries.hero_structure: NEW: THE CHILD'S EYE LINE. One continuous nursery floor under one camera that dollies steadily right across nine frames, with a single soft toy at full close range on the cover, receding to a distant silhouette by the breather, and returning large and near on the close. Everything the deck knows lies ON that floor as loose sheets of paper, and each sheet's treatment IS the deck's grammar: a sheet stamped READ is a record that was actually fetched, a sheet stamped 403 or NOT PUBLISHED is one that was refused or does not exist. Diverges from THE EQUAL-AWARD PROJECTION (33) by having a camera, an object, a room and a floor where that had none of the four; from THE LOCKED CHASE (32) by being soft, warm-lit and in motion where that was rigid, wet and square on; from THE FALLING FRAME (31) by holding one continuous ground plane instead of dropping the frame; and from THE OPEN TREAD (30) by making the ROOM incidental and the PAPER the subject.

entries.note: Six art prototypes (P0-P5) were built and run through the real gates BEFORE any dossier was written, and their findings were binding on all nine. P2 established that a smooth PBR ground fails frame_balance for want of per-cell luminance spread and that hanging a procedural canvas texture on the ground material fixes it. P3 proved that scattering marks to satisfy the gate ruins the picture, and was recorded as the wrong answer. Phase 12 then found that scripts/bespoke_check.py could not see <script type='module'> at all, so every akthree deck had been measured on its <div> list alone; the repair is what turned this deck's reported 0.810 median and 0 percent drawn share into the honest 0.368 and 72 percent above. REVISED AFTER THE SCORE ROUNDS: the toy does NOT leave the frame by the end; it is large and near again on 09, which is the close returning to the cover's distance. Two claimed repairs had to be made twice because the first attempt treated a symptom. The weave was minified below one screen pixel, so anisotropy and a bump map could not reach it and only a larger texture footprint could. Slide 05's grille was under the copy reserve, which is painted after the GL composite, so no material change could ever have lit it.
